B1: correct reason given — "angle in a semicircle is 90°" (or equivalent reference to AB being a diameter)

questions.topic_aspect: Angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference
questions.mark_scheme:
M1: State/use circle theorem — angle at centre = 2 × angle at circumference (angle AOB = 2 × angle ACB)
M1: Correct equation formed: 136 = 2 × angle ACB
A1: Angle ACB = 68° (correct final answer, halving not doubling)
questions.misconception_targeted: Halving instead of doubling, or applying to wrong arc

questions.topic_aspect: Cyclic quadrilateral - opposite angles sum to 180
questions.mark_scheme:
M1: Correct equation formed using opposite angles sum to 180° (3x + x + 52 = 180)
M1: Correct rearrangement/simplification to solve for x (4x = 128 or equivalent), leading to x = 32
A1: Both correct final angles stated — angle BAD = 96° and angle BCD = 84° (ft from their x if equation method correct)
questions.misconception_targeted: Assuming opposite angles are equal rather than supplementary
